whats_working: Clean, consistent use of shared primitives (StatusBanner, Card, ScreenHeader, Badge, MetricCard, AppButton) — the screen hand-rolls almost no bespoke styling, so tokens/spacing stay coherent across all four platforms.

Dark mode is well tuned: hero, metric tiles and the offline card all sit on distinct surface tokens (#1E201C surface vs #141513 bg) with legible foreground, and the sync banner keeps its soft-green tint.
The bottom action bar keeps the two CTAs at 52pt height with comfortable thumb-zone placement and clear primary/secondary contrast (solid green vs bordered neutral).

State reflection is honest and useful: draft state swaps eyebrow labels (Continue survey / Resume audit), shows Score 6% and a 'Saved on Cloud / Draft saved Jul 4 2:15 AM' timestamp — good Feedback and Findable signalling.

findings.title: not_started sync label + badge use the warning FILL token as text on a light surface (fails AA)
findings.affected: app/(tabs)/execute.tsx:100-103,140-146 (tone from getPlaceStatusTone) + hero syncLabel Paragraph style={{color: tone.text}}
findings.evidence: iphone/light/07-execute.png and android-tablet/light/05-execute.png: the hero line 'Ready for offline capture' and the 'NOT STARTED' badge render as pale gold. getPlaceStatusTone(not_started) returns {text: colors.warning} = #C89A57; on surface #FFFFFF that is ~2.4:1, below AA 4.5:1. DESIGN.md rule: fill tokens (warning) must not be used as text on soft backgrounds — use warningText #8A5F16.
findings.why: The primary status headline for a not-started place is the lowest-contrast text on the screen in light mode; auditors scanning readiness may miss it, and it violates the design system's own token rule.
findings.fix: In getPlaceStatusTone, split fill vs text: return text: colors.warningText (#8A5F16) for the not_started tone (and successText/dangerText for the others) so tone.text is AA-safe; the badge Badge component already needs the *Text token too. Keep the fill (warning) only for the accent/surface.

findings.title: Both footer buttons navigate to the exact same route for not_started/draft
findings.evidence: Secondary 'Start survey' calls openAuditForPlace(id) -> router.push(`/audit/${id}/1`). Primary 'Open audit' calls the same openAuditForPlace(id) except when isSubmitted. So in every not_started (07 screenshots) and draft (dark 07) state, the two visually-distinct buttons land on identical destination.
findings.why: Two side-by-side CTAs with different labels but one behavior is a false choice — it makes the user stop and think which is 'right', and undermines the primary/secondary hierarchy that the button styling promises.
findings.fix: For non-submitted states show a single full-width primary AppButton ('Start survey' / 'Resume audit'); reserve the two-button row only for submitted places (Open report vs re-open). Or give the secondary a genuinely distinct action (e.g. view place details / directions).

findings.title: Tablet is a stretched phone layout: content-light detail spans the full width with a large empty canvas
findings.evidence: ipad/light/05-execute.png & android-tablet/light/05-execute.png: three cards fill the ~1024pt width with roughly the bottom two-thirds of the screen empty; the offline paragraph 'Your responses are saved on this device and will sync when you are back online.' runs one long ~90-character line. No maxWidth is passed, so it defaults to contentMaxWidth (1040–1200), but responsive-layout.ts guidance is that content-light detail (Execute) should cap at readableMaxWidth 760.
findings.why: Long line lengths hurt readability, the wide short cards look unfinished, and the vast dead space signals the screen was never adapted to the large canvas — a tablet-only regression versus the tidy phone layout.
findings.fix: Pass maxWidth: 760 (readableMaxWidth) to getResponsiveContentContainerStyle so the column centers; or introduce a proper two-pane/master-detail (place list on the left rail, this detail on the right) to use the canvas, per the responsive-layout master-detail pattern.

findings.title: Absolute footer uses raw screen padding, not the content track — will misalign if content is centered
findings.evidence: The footer XStack pins left/right to layout.screenPaddingHorizontal while the ScrollView content uses getResponsiveContentContainerStyle (which switches to adaptive centered gutters on wide tablets). On the captured iPad width the two happen to coincide (content is edge-to-edge), but as soon as the fix above centers content at 760/1040, the footer will no longer align to the track. Core guidance: footers align to the track via getContentTrackInnerWidth().
findings.why: The footer is the primary action surface; a mismatch between its edges and the content column reads as broken alignment on larger tablets and split-view widths.
findings.fix: Compute the footer's horizontal insets from getContentTrackInnerWidth(layout, maxWidth) (center a maxWidth-wide row) instead of layout.screenPaddingHorizontal, so it tracks the content column across all breakpoints.

findings.title: 'Ready for offline capture' appears twice on the same screen
findings.evidence: iphone/light/07-execute.png (and every not_started capture): the hero shows 'Ready for offline capture / Not started yet' and, two cards below, a separate card repeats the bold header 'Ready for offline capture'. Same phrase twice within one viewport.
findings.why: Repeating identical phrasing wastes vertical space, dilutes the meaning of the phrase, and blurs the hierarchy between the place-status headline and the offline-storage explainer.
findings.fix: Differentiate the two: keep the hero's status line status-specific (e.g. 'Not started' as the bold line) and reword the bottom card header to describe the storage guarantee ('Saved on this device') so the two blocks carry distinct information.

findings.title: Hero card leaves the entire right half empty on tablet
findings.affected: app/(tabs)/execute.tsx:131-154 (Card with ScreenHeader; badge floats top-right)
findings.evidence: ipad/light/05-execute.png & ipad/dark/05-execute.png: the hero Card is full-width but all content (eyebrow, title, sync label) hugs the left; the badge sits top-right and the right ~55% of the card is blank.
findings.why: On the large canvas the hero looks unbalanced and reinforces the impression of an un-adapted phone card.
findings.fix: Once the content column is capped (see tablet-no-adaptation finding) this largely resolves; optionally move the score/metrics or a place thumbnail into the right of the hero on tablet to balance the composition.

findings.title: Scrolled state renders the 'Execute' title under the status-bar clock on iPhone
findings.affected: app/(tabs)/execute.tsx:120-128 ScrollView contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior='automatic'; top padding only screenPaddingVertical (no topInset)
findings.evidence: iphone/light/08-execute-detail.png and iphone/dark/08-execute-detail.png: the bold 'Execute' title overlaps the 2:10 / 2:17 status-bar clock and Dynamic Island. The tab screens have no stack header, and the content-container top padding is just screenPaddingVertical (16) with no safe-area topInset passed; contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior='automatic' may not apply here.
findings.why: If the header can sit under the notch/clock it is a safe-area regression; even as a transient scroll frame it shows the top inset is not reserved by the layout itself.
findings.fix: Pass topInset: useSafeAreaInsets().top into getResponsiveContentContainerStyle (it already accepts topInset), or wrap the header in a SafeAreaView edge='top', so the title always clears the status bar independent of scroll offset.
